transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning check-in for the spring musical. As we work through the production plan together, I want to make sure we address all the key areas before I give my final approval. The draft currently proposes a Friday 7:00 p.m. performance with 220 seats, ordinary stage effects, and optional recording. I'd like to hear from each of you regarding any concerns or adjustments you think we need to make. Let's start with your thoughts on the proposed schedule and seating.

transcript.text: I need to raise an important issue before we finalize anything. The rights holder for one of the musical numbers in our show confirmed to me by email this week that the school may perform it only after purchasing a live-performance license, and that any audio or video recording of the production is prohibited. I haven't yet attached that email to the activity-approval file, but I'm bringing it to everyone's attention now because it directly affects the draft plan's proposal for optional event recording.

transcript.text: I need to flag a seating concern before we go any further. I completed the facilities inspection for the auditorium this week, and I found that we may seat exactly 160 audience members for this production — not the 220 currently in the draft plan. Additionally, both marked side exits must remain clear. I haven't yet updated the draft seating plan to reflect these findings, but everyone needs to know this now since it directly affects the proposed seating number.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical health and safety concern. A cast member has a documented severe latex allergy, which I confirmed in the student's health record this week. This means all props and costume materials used in the production must be latex-free, and a staff member trained in the school's emergency-allergy protocol must be present at every performance. I haven't yet added this to the production file, but everyone needs to know this now so we can build it into the final plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical scheduling concern. The district activity-bus coordinator confirmed that 12 participating students cannot reliably obtain evening transportation, and that an activity bus is available for a Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee. I confirmed this with the affected families and the transportation office this week. This means the Friday evening performance must be moved to the Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee — not supplemented with an additional performance. I haven't yet entered this in the event calendar, but everyone needs to know this now so we can adjust the final schedule accordingly.
